PERSONAL DEV FLEET · THE VISION & WHERE WE STAND · 2026-07-23

Your Dev Server Grows a Fleet

Vision + status report · 2026-07-23 · epic personal-dev-fleet-epic

You don't buy a fleet. Your dev server grows one — one support at a time. One personal machine stays your home base; helper machines exist only to serve it, absorbing the heavy work so your main never slows down. This paper is the vision first, the build status second.

What we are creating

The main is your dev server — a Personal Dev Server running Barkpark, Studio, Chat, and the central task ledger. It is where you live: your data, your papers, your tasks, your chat. Around it grow supports: machines that are subordinate by design. They hold no data of their own, run no Barkpark of their own — they listen to your ledger, claim heavy work off it, do the work, and report back. Kill one and nothing of yours is lost.

Why machines and not threads, containers, or worktrees? Because we measured it: one agent melting a box starves every neighbour on it. Worktrees isolate code; only a machine isolates performance. The unit of isolation is the machine — that is the doctrine the whole product stands on.

The whole idea in one line

The winning strategy
The ledger is the bus. A fence is a lease. Presence is a heartbeat. The router is best-fit. The machine is the isolation boundary.

Everything else is elaboration. Workers speak four verbs to the ledger — claim, pulse, stamp, close — and the system extends on three axes without ever changing the protocol: add a listener, add a one-line agent adapter, add an order type. It is provider-neutral by construction: any agent with a shell can join. Claude and Codex have both already completed the contract live, on the same ledger.

What it feels like to use

The MVP is not an API — it is a journey you can see in the Cloud console. Four clicks, one feeling:

A support goes online — and starts billing — only on its first heartbeat: a box stuck provisioning never lies and never charges. A spend cap is not a warning, it is a brake: cap hit means ambition drops to zero and dispatch freezes.

The product ladder

RungWhat you getPrice
Personal LocalThe whole fleet protocol on your own hardware — full capability, foreverFree
Personal Dev ServerYour main in the cloud: Barkpark + Studio + Chat + ledger, managed$29/mo
FleetThe same $29 rung growing — each support is an add-on line item, sized per task class+ per support

Paid buys convenience, never capability — the free local fleet must always remain possible. That is inherited law, not marketing.

Where we are: the build

The epic runs in proven waves — every wave ships a proof that must fire, plus a negative control proving the proof can fail. Two of five epic criteria are sealed; the third wave is in its live-fire round as this is written.

MilestoneMeaningStatus
PresenceWorkers are visible: register, heartbeat, and a dead worker shows OFFLINE exactly at its TTLSEALED — kill-a-listener proof 7/7
EfficiencyRouting is measured, never guessed: heavy work lands on big boxes, light on lean, and the spend cap freezes dispatchSEALED — efficiency proof 9/9
GrowthOne action grows the fleet: bp cloud support add provisions, binds, scrubs, starts a listener; remove tears all of it down to census-zeroVerbs merged at grade A; live fire running now on a real box
Stranger journeySomeone who is not us walks create → add → offload unaided in the consoleNext after Wave C
DurabilityThe fence-lifecycle bug dies; lease-lapse recovery provenFiled, waiting
The sealOne unattended mixed-agent, mixed-size run completes a real wish with honest gradesThe finish line

Today's live fire (Cycle 7): the round-3 proof provisions one real Hetzner box through the one-action verb, watches it come online in the roster with measured capacity, proves the pulled data is scrubbed to zero secrets, proves a stuck box never lies online, then removes it and shows all four surfaces — box, roster, bind, token — at census delta zero.

The living ledger

The epic's children, straight from the task system — this list is live and updates as work closes:

tasks — No tasks yet.
Verdict
The vision is stable and the substrate is proven: a personal main that grows measured, disposable helpers over one four-verb protocol. What remains is honesty under fire — a real box today, a stranger tomorrow, an unattended run at the end. No new invention required; only proofs that must fire.
